name: Heavy aggregates never take the service down — regression-hardening golden reading GET /api/health-backed attributes and persisted data_provider_runs fields, never a bare page-title/heading match

steps.title: TC-8 — GET /api/health is answering live: the readiness badge's OWN data-state attribute reads ready, not a heading/title match
The background-compute panel (fed by the SAME GET /api/health poll's background_compute field) discloses a real, non-fabricated state
A persisted data_provider_runs status field renders — the finalize tail's own recorded outcome, not a live/fabricated state
TC-5/TC-8 — the SAME persisted aggregates_refreshed field the finalize tail's heavy warm writes (coverage/membership_timeline/market_phase/forward_aggregates/... per aggregates_refreshed)

_notes: ops-hardening iter-54 (T4/TC-8). J-07's own full behavior — a live forward-aggregate warm across every horizon, GET /api/health polled 1/s throughout, VmPeak measured, a fault-injected memory-pressure abort — is proven by the dedicated live concurrent drill (reports/perf-budgets.md, this iteration's dated addendum, and its predecessors Addenda 13/14/15), NOT by this script: demo_runner.py is pure browser automation (goto/click/fill/wait_for/expect only, no process-control or raw-HTTP-timing action type — apps/backend/scripts/automation/lib/demo_runner.py's `_do_action`), so a multi-minute concurrent-polling scenario cannot be reproduced deterministically inside a Playwright replay.

This golden's scope, honestly stated: a FAST, deterministic regression check that the browser-visible surfaces J-07's acceptance criteria depend on are genuinely wired to GET /api/health and to persisted data_provider_runs rows, never a static shell. Step 2 reads the readiness badge's data-state ATTRIBUTE (apps/frontend/components/health-badge.tsx) via a CSS attribute selector — this can only read 'ready' if GET /api/health actually answered with state:"ready", closing the iter-52 lesson ('assert a value the endpoint must have produced, not a heading the shell renders'). Steps 4-5 read `apps/frontend/app/data/page.tsx`'s `LastRunSummary`/`BackfillBreakdown` — the TC-6/ops-hardening-iter-1 reduced persisted-run view, built from `DataRun` (data_provider_runs) fields only — WITHOUT triggering a new live job (J-05's golden already covers a fresh live backfill's own aggregates_refreshed write; this golden proves the READ side survives cold, on a page load with no live job in this browser session).

Step 5 (aggregates-refreshed) depends on the MOST RECENT persisted run (GET /api/data's recent_runs[0]) having a non-empty aggregates_refreshed list — true after any normal fetch/backfill/rebuild run (this iteration's own live concurrent drill, task per the dev handoff, creates exactly such a run). A zero-work run (e.g. a weekend-only span, or a fetch/expand-only job) can leave this field empty/omitted (`BackfillBreakdown`'s documented all-null-renders-nothing convention) — if the replay lane's most recent run happens to be zero-work, re-run after any real backfill, or rotate this step out; not treated as flaky-and-ignored, named here per this project's honesty convention.

ops-hardening iter-58 (browser-qa-agent): re-verified all five steps live against the shipped tree — readiness-badge read data-state="ready", background-compute-panel showed a REAL in-flight warm (asof-key 2026-07-31, dataset r2948-f6549680, horizons 1/5, elapsed climbing) that this pass happened to catch already running, not one this golden or the QA pass triggered. That warm's own 1Hz GET /api/health poll (229 samples, 19:49:19Z-19:54:16Z, reports/qa/goal-ops-hardening-iter-58-evidence/j07-health-poll.log) recorded 0 non-200 throughout, INCLUDING through the moment the warm itself hit a genuine MemoryError (VmPeak pegged exactly at the 8192 MB `server.memory_cap_mb` ulimit -v ceiling; GET /api/health's own `background_compute.recent_outcomes` honestly recorded `outcome:"failed"` at 1/5 horizons, duration_ms 639027) and a concurrent GET /api/research/regime-lab request raised a raw MemoryError (traceback in logs/backend.log). The SAME process (pid 782444) kept serving normally afterward with no restart — confirmed directly by this same QA pass's own J-05 backfill completing cleanly on it minutes later. This is live, unplanned, real evidence for the acceptance clause 'a memory-pressure abort never leaves the process wedged... health/readiness stay truthful throughout' (step 4's property), even though this golden's own steps 1-5 do not and cannot reproduce a multi-minute concurrent-compute scenario (see the iter-54 note above, still true). Lint clean; no step text changed.
